messages:
taylor: Heads-up — saw a tail-latency spike on the canary for llama3-13b when chat-template enabled. pattern: short user prompts + long system prompt -> Kv cache churn + kernel selector flips. attaching quick profile.

sam: ugh. can you paste the perf snippet? also which kernel flip, fused <-> fallback?

taylor: perf snippet (nvprof style):
```
GPU active time: 92.1ms
kernel_selector.cpp: 43.7% CPU
kv_cache_manager: 21.2% CPU
memcpy H2D: 5.9ms
context switch (kernel swap): 1.2ms per request tail
tail p99: 312ms (baseline 285ms)
```
Observed frequent selector decisions at seq_len ~48-72 causing small-run fused kernel to be chosen then falling back for vcache hits. leads to micro-thrashing on the GPU and extra memcpy.

viv: interesting — that fits a batching heuristic boundary. our selector uses `threshold_seq=64` currently; chat templates add ~40 tokens prefix, so many requests land in the flip zone. also rope_theta defaults can change memory addressing for kv which affects prefetch heuristics.

sam: can we force a consistent kernel for those chat-template flows? quick experiment ideas:
- prefer_fused=true for seq<128
- increase prefetch pages to avoid H2D bursts
- pin eviction to keep recent prefixes

perf-bot: :warning: regression-detect-bot detected +2.4% p99 latency vs baseline on canary (2026-03-18T08:21Z) — details: https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/3088881234

taylor: tried a local patch: 
```
runtime.selector.prefer_fused = true
runtime.selector.threshold_seq = 128
kv.prefetch.pages = 3
kv.eviction.policy = "lru_keep_prefix"
```
Result: p99 improved from 312ms -> 293ms, throughput -1.2%, tail variance reduced. CPU kernel_selector time dropped ~15%.

viv: good. I think longer-term we should avoid discrete threshold flips: add hysteresis to selector (sticky choice for N requests per session) and expose chat-template adapter that advertises effective prefix_len so selector can bias decisions.

sam: agree. also let's add telemetry tags: `chat_template:true`, `effective_prefix_len`, `selector_choice` so we can roll metrics and not guess.

taylor: I'll open a small RFC and a canary feature flag: `stable_kernel_for_chat_templates`. plan: 1) quick canary with prefer_fused+prefetch 2) add selector hysteresis (sticky for 30s per session) 3) telemetry. assigning tasks.

viv: assign viv -> selector hysteresis PR, taylor -> canary config + telemetry, sam -> rollout criteria + perf dashboard update. 

sam: ping @eng-sre for canary burn window. :thumbsup:

taylor: thanks — leaving logs in #eng-runtime-archives and tagging the PR in the thread when ready.
